name: State Trading Corporation Building
features: Vierendeel trusses and Mughal-inspired polychrome sandstone cladding; Metabolist influence.

photos.file: File:State Trading Corporation building, New Delhi.jpg

note: Only one free photo found; good daylight exterior. Built 1976-89. Office type but a key Rewal work.

name: Vigyan Bhawan
features: Plenary hall seating over 1,200 delegates, six smaller halls, and a central atrium.

photos.file: File:East gate of Vigyan Bhawan Delhi P 20170403 094024 01.jpg

note: Second photo shows the east gateway with people and signs; first is the better exterior.

name: Supreme Court of India
features: Plan meant to resemble the scales of justice; central wing under a 27.6 m dome with a colonnaded verandah.

photos.file: File:Supreme Court of India front view 05.jpg

note: Lead photo is only 800px wide (nothing better found; others are through railings, dusk). Year is when the court moved in (1958) per Wikipedia; foundation 1954, wings added 1979 and 1994. Wikipedia calls the style Indo-British.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium
by: Gerkan, Marg and Partners (2010 redesign); roof by Schlaich Bergermann Partner
features: 53,800 m2 PTFE-membrane roof carried on about 8,500 tonnes of steel; original stadium 1982.

photos.file: File:Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium Delhi outside view, July 2016.jpg

note: Photo is a distant view from a road, hazy; weak. Year is the 2010 renovation (original built 1982, architect not named in article). Reviewer: maybe look for a better photo.

name: Bharat Mandapam
features: 390,000 m2 convention centre with a 7,000-seat hall and six exhibition halls; retrofuturist style.
note: Second photo is an evening view across a fountain pool.

name: Virasat-e-Khalsa
features: Honey-coloured stone and steel-clad double-curved roofs around an artificial lake; turrets grouped in fives.
note: Inaugurated 25 Nov 2011 (article gives no separate completion date).

name: A. C. Joshi Library, Panjab University
features: Central library on Jeanneret's chequerboard campus plan; foundation 1958, inaugurated 1963.

photos.file: File:The Central Library, Panjab University, Chandigarh.jpg
File:AC JOSHI LIBRARY PANJAB UNIVERSITY CHANDIGARH.jpg

note: Facts from the Panjab University article (Central Library, Jeanneret, inaugurated 1963). The article does not describe the facade. Second photo is a dusk shot with a person in frame.

name: Yashobhoomi (India International Convention and Expo Centre)
by: C P Kukreja Architects, IDOM and ARCOP Associates
features: 1 km-long foyer linking the halls, convertible auditorium seating, rainwater harvesting; IGBC Green Cities Platinum.

photos.file: File:Yashobhoomi – India International Convention and Expo Centre, Delhi.jpg

note: First phase opened 17 Sep 2023. Other category photos not viewed.

name: Raj Mandir Cinema
features: Art Moderne cinema with a meringue-shaped auditorium and nine stars for the Navaratna gems.
note: Photo has street crowd and posters; movement chosen Art Deco as nearest vocab to Art Moderne.

name: Swaminarayan Akshardham
by: BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha with Virendra Trivedi
features: Pink sandstone and Carrara marble, no steel or concrete; 234 carved pillars and nine domes.
note: New (2005) temple in traditional Maru-Gurjara style.

name: Humayun's Tomb
by: Mirak Mirza Ghiyas and Sayyid Muhammad
features: Double dome on a high drum; red sandstone with white marble, the first such combination at this scale in India.
note: Photo shows a corner of the tomb with the dome behind, hazy; one photo only (others in the search not viewed).

name: Hawa Mahal
features: Five-storey pyramid of red and pink sandstone with 953 small latticed jharokha windows.

photos.file: File:East facade of the Hawa Mahal, Jaipur.jpg

note: Photo is a close crop of the facade, not the whole building; the whole-front photos were not retrievable.

name: Amer Fort
features: Red sandstone and marble on four levels, each with a courtyard; Sukh Niwas cooled by water channels.

photos.file: File:Exterior View of Amer Fort, Jaipur, Rajasthan.JPG

note: Second photo is a floodlit evening view.

name: ISKCON Temple (Glory of India)
features: One of the largest temple complexes in India, with a 375-seat auditorium and a Vedic cultural centre.
note: Photo is 1494px wide; Kanvinde took the project pro bono (1993).

name: New Parliament Building
by: Bimal Patel (HCP Design, Planning and Management)
features: Triangular plan beside the old Parliament; separate Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha chambers and a central Constitution Hall.
note: no free photo: Commons files found are all GODL-India.

name: National War Memorial
features: Four concentric circles (chakravyuh) around a central obelisk with eternal flame; ring of trees.
note: no good daylight photo seen: the ones I viewed were night shots or people-filled; many CC BY-SA files exist in the category for a reviewer to check.

name: Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar Memorial Park
features: Red sandstone memorial on 108 acres; 124 elephant statues flank the entrance, with an 80-foot pyramid-type structure.
note: no good daylight photo seen: viewed ones were night or dusk. Many large CC BY-SA files exist in the category (about 40+) for a reviewer to check.

name: National Museum, New Delhi
features: Three floors of galleries radiating from a central garden court; planned in phases toward an octagon.
note: no free photo found of the building exterior (category is mostly museum objects).

name: National Centre for the Performing Arts
features: Concrete-frame International Style arts complex on reclaimed land at Nariman Point; concept by Philip Johnson.

photos.file: File:Jamshed Bhabha Theatre at NCPA, Mumbai.jpg

note: Wikipedia: completed 1985, opened 1986; Tata Theatre opened 1982. Only the Jamshed Bhabha Theatre block seen; other photos unseen/rate-limited.

name: Visvesvaraya Centre (VV Towers)
features: Two concrete towers of 22 and 12 storeys joined by a three-storey podium; Brutalist style.
note: Office type (government offices) but a Correa Brutalist key work; the only ordinary-type entry. Trees partly screen other faces.

name: St. Peter and St. Paul's Church, Parumala
features: Circular plan, 39 m inner diameter, split into three segments by two 16 m chords; seats over 2,000.
note: Year 2000 from the Charles Correa article; church article gives 1895 for the older foundation.

name: Chowdiah Memorial Hall
features: 1,100-seat auditorium built in the shape of a gigantic seven-stringed violin; completed 1980.
note: Only one free exterior photo found (2816x2112), hazy light and the violin form is not obvious from this angle.

name: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Telangana State Secretariat
by: Ponni Concessao and Oscar Concessao (OCI Architects)
features: Domed Indo-Saracenic-style secretariat, 265 ft tall, with 635 rooms on a 27.9-acre site.

photos.file: File:Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Telangana State Secretariat complex in Hyderabad.jpg

note: Opened 30 April 2023; main contractor Shapoorji Pallonji.

name: Jehangir Art Gallery
features: One of the city's early concrete buildings, with a large wavy cantilevered entrance canopy; four exhibition halls.
note: Wikipedia credits Durga Bajpai in the Architecture section but G. M. Bhuta (citation needed) in the lead: reviewer to check.

name: Valluvar Kottam
features: 39 m granite temple-chariot monument with a Valluvar statue; Kural couplets carved around the auditorium hall.

name: Antilia
features: 27-storey, 173 m private residence, designed to withstand a magnitude-eight earthquake.
note: Private residence; built 2006-2010 per Wikipedia. Photo is distant and hazy but clear.

name: Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre
features: Arts centre in Jio World Centre with a 2,000-seat Grand Theatre, a Studio Theatre, a Cube and a four-storey Art House.
note: no free photo in good light: the only file in the article and my search is a night shot with signage (File:2023-0329-nmacc-night.jpg, CC0); reviewer may check the Commons category for daylight exteriors.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (Victoria Terminus)
by: Frederick William Stevens (from an initial design by Axel Haig)
features: Indo-Saracenic and Victorian Gothic Revival railway terminus with 18 platforms; UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2004.
note: Infobox gives 20 May 1888; text says completed 1887, opened to public 1888. Historic precedent #2 of 4.

name: Victoria Memorial
features: Indo-Saracenic memorial-museum in white Makrana marble, in 26 hectares of gardens, opened in 1921.
note: Historic precedent #3 of 4.

name: Vidhana Soudha
features: Neo-Dravidian legislature building in Karnataka granite; four floors, 172 rooms, motto carved on the entablature.

photos.file: File:Vidhana Soudha (Bengaluru) - View of the central dome and front portico with the motto inscription.jpg

note: Photo is a close view of the central dome and portico, not the whole facade. Finished 1956 (built 1952-56).

name: Nehru Centre
features: Cylindrical tower on a sloped, landscaped base; 1,000-seat auditorium, planetarium, exhibition galleries.
note: Completed 1985 on a six-acre Worli site; foundation stone 1972.

name: Gateway of India
features: 26 m yellow basalt and reinforced-concrete arch, Indo-Saracenic, drawing on 16th-century Gujarati architecture.
note: Historic precedent #1 of 4. Photo is whole building in daylight but with crowds, barriers and pigeons in front; a cleaner file may exist in the category (not seen).

name: Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR)
features: Jakkur campus with Correa's Buckyball structure at the Molecular Biology and Genetics Unit; inaugurated 1995.
commons_category: Category:Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research
note: no free photo: Commons category holds only the Buckyball interior view and a gazebo; no exterior of the campus buildings.

name: Anna Centenary Library
features: Nine-floor library on 8 acres holding 1.2 million books; first library building in Asia with LEED NC Gold.
note: Opened 15 September 2010 per infobox.

name: Ravindra Bharathi
features: Auditorium of about 1,000 seats built for Tagore's birth centenary; opened 1961 and renovated in 2005.
note: Architect name spelled Mohammed (infobox) / Mohammad (text) in the article. Movement Modernism is my reading of 1960s date, not stated by the source.

name: Swaminarayan Akshardham, Gandhinagar
features: 108 ft main temple in about 6,000 tonnes of pink Rajasthan sandstone, 97 carved pillars and 17 domes; no steel used.
note: Only photo in the article is 1140x735 (long side under 1200px); Commons category name not found, a larger file may exist. Infobox 2 Nov 1992, inaugurated 4 Nov 1992.

name: Sidi Saiyyed Mosque
by: Shaikh Sa'id Al-Habshi Sultani (Sidi Sa'id), builder
features: Ten carved stone latticework windows (jalis); the Sidi Saiyyed Jali is an unofficial symbol of Ahmedabad.

photos.file: File:Front view of Sidi Saiyyed Mosque, Ahmedabad.jpg

note: Historic precedent #4 of 4. Article names the builder, not an architect; built 980 AH (1572/73). The jali itself is not in the two seen photos (see Commons category).

name: Biswa Bangla Gate (Kolkata Gate)
features: 55 m gate: a circular viewing ring carried by two parabolic arches on four legs; about 70 tonnes of steel.

photos.file: File:Kolkata Gate (officially known as Biswa Bangla Gate).jpg

note: Completed 27 Jan 2018, opened 2 Feb 2019. Only usable photo is a heavily saturated sunset shot; the architect is given as the firm Vector Designs.

name: Mahindra United World College of India
features: Hilltop campus of 'wadas' (student house clusters around courtyards) in local materials, near Mulshi Dam.
note: Year is the inauguration (28 Nov 1997); the article gives no completion year. Photo 1936x1113 shows stone-clad buildings along a path, not the whole campus.

name: Nandan
features: Government film and cultural centre with three auditoria (931, 200 and 100 seats); logo designed by Satyajit Ray.
note: Inaugurated 2 Sept 1985. Photo is taken at dusk with people in front; other files in the category are similar or event shots. Architect is only in the infobox.

name: DakshinaChitra
features: Living-history museum of 18 relocated heritage houses; Baker's free master plan rejected a big exhibition pavilion.
note: no free photo of the museum buildings themselves: Commons files show relocated heritage houses (Kerala House, etc.), not Baker/Kuriakose architecture; reviewer to decide. Opened 14 Dec 1996.

name: Calico Dome
features: Five-pointed geodesic-inspired dome, described as India's first space frame structure; collapsed and under restoration.
note: no free photo: Wikipedia article has none and the Commons category listing returned empty; dates conflict in the article (infobox 1962, text 1963).

name: Ranga Shankara
features: 320-seat theatre in J.P. Nagar built for about 3 crore, raised mainly through public contributions.
note: Opened 28 Oct 2004. Photo is the street front in daylight with festival signage in front.

name: Vidyasagar Setu (Second Hooghly Bridge)
features: Cable-stayed bridge over the Hooghly: 822.96 m long, 457.2 m main span, steel pylons 127.62 m tall.
note: no good photo seen: tried a deck view in cloud, a hazy deck view and a sunset silhouette (File:Vidyasagar Setu 2010.jpg); the category has 56 files, a daylight side view probably exists but was not seen. Opened 10 Oct 1992.

name: Bandaranaike Memorial International Conference Hall
features: Chinese-designed gift to Sri Lanka; a colonnaded hall in Cinnamon Gardens, built 1970-73.
note: Only one seen photo (front elevation, daylight). Other free file BMICH for ACD 8.jpg (PD, 3072px) would not load, left out.

name: Nelum Pokuna Mahinda Rajapaksa Theatre
features: Performing-arts theatre inspired by the 12th-century Nelum Pokuna lotus pond at Polonnaruwa.

photos.file: File:04 Colombo (42) Gledališče Nelum Pokuna Mahinda Rajapaksa.jpg

name: Sunethra Bandaranaike House
features: Bawa's conversion of old stables into a house with a new wing, forming an L shape; built 1983-87.
note: One photo, seen: white house with tiled roofs behind frangipani trees; file title says residence at Horagolla. Reviewer please confirm it shows the Bawa wing/stables.

name: Martyred Intellectuals Memorial
by: Farid Uddin Ahmed and Md Jami-al-Shafi
features: Long curved brick wall about 17.7 m tall, broken at the ends to show grief, recalling the Rayer Bazar brickfield.
note: Lead photo is black and white but shows the wall and steps.

name: Mausoleum of Three Leaders
by: Masud Ahmad and S. A. Zahiruddin
features: Shell-like roof of a hyperbolic paraboloid structure raised over the three graves.
note: Another file 'Mausoleum of three leaders 3.jpg' (5000x3333) was seen as grave inscription close up, not used.

name: Narayanhiti Palace Museum
features: Royal palace using Nepalese building styles as a national symbol; designed by Benjamin Polk, begun 1963.

name: Singha Durbar
by: Kumar Narsingh Rana and Kishor Narsingh Rana
features: Rana-era palace built in 1908, described as a unique merging of building traditions.
note: Both photos hazy, long views; second is public domain 1984x1488.

name: Sigiriya
features: Fifth-century rock-top palace and fortress with a lion gateway and symmetrical water gardens on an east-west axis.
note: Year = end of Kashyapa's reign 477-495 CE. Aerial/stair photo seen but not used.

name: Sixty Dome Mosque
features: Brick mosque with thick tapered walls in Tughlaq style and a hut-shaped roof; built 1442-1459.

name: Somapura Mahavihara
features: Quadrangular Buddhist monastery of 177 cells around a central stupa; Dharmapala reigned c. 781-821 CE.
note: Year approximate (c. 800).

name: Lankatilaka Vihara
features: 14th-century temple on a rock, designed by South Indian architect Sathapati Rayar for Bhuvanekabahu IV.
note: Built in the reign of Bhuvanekabahu IV (1341-1351); year given as end of reign.

name: Hatirjheel
features: Lake and waterfront public space in central Dhaka, opened in 2013; design team led by Iqbal Habib.
note: Seen photo shows one of the arched bridges and the lake in daylight; project is a landscape/infrastructure, reviewer may judge it out of scope.

name: Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Novo Theatre
features: Planetarium on Bijoy Sarani Avenue, Tejgaon, designed by Ali Imam; opened September 2004.

photos.file: File:Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Novo Theatre (02).jpg

note: Seen: glazed dome with steel frame, columned wings, daylight, hazy sky.

name: Bishop's College, Colombo (Bawa classroom block)
features: Three-storey classroom block with an open ground level; classrooms on the first and second floors.
note: no free photo (Commons has none; Wikipedia article has only a crest). Wikipedia says Bawa and Plesner were engaged in 1959; Bawa list gives 1960-1963.

name: Blue Water Hotel
features: Rest-house layout first used at Serendib Hotel (1967), scaled up with large courtyards and a screening wall.
note: no free photo: the only file (Coconut trees and pool.jpg) shows pool and palms, not the building's exterior.

name: Pradeep Jayewardene House
features: Rectangular main building 34 m long and 12 m wide on a hilltop overlooking the bay.
note: no free photo found on Commons.

name: Zebun Nessa Mosque
features: Square base surrounding a circular prayer hall; led by Saiqa Iqbal Meghna.
note: no free photo found on Commons (searches empty).

name: Supreme Court of Pakistan Building
features: Stepped white blocks with a deep colonnaded portico on Constitution Avenue; Neoclassical and Modernist blend.

photos.file: File:Supreme Court of Pakistan, Islamabad by Usman Ghani.jpg

note: Wikipedia credits Kenzo Tange with the Pakistan EPA. Photos found by Commons search, no category given.

name: Aiwan-e-Sadr (Presidential Palace)
features: Modern step-pyramid form with four main halls set in Mughal-style gardens; large rooftop solar system.
note: Only the aerial is seen and shows the palace in its setting; ground-level shots tried were hazy or failed to load.

name: Pakistan National Art Gallery
by: Suhail Abbasi and Naeem Pasha (Suhail & Pasha)
features: Four-storey brick cube with 14 galleries, lecture halls and a 400-seat auditorium; won a 1989 design contest.

name: Islamic Summit Minar
features: 47 m marble and stone obelisk beside a reflecting pool, with an underground museum, for the 1974 Islamic Summit.

name: Lahore Expo Centre
by: NESPAK with Nayyar Ali Dada & Associates
features: Convention centre in Johar Town with exhibition halls and a convention hall holding two auditoriums.
note: Photo file name says Expo Center Lahore; dusk shot of brick arcades. Reviewer: confirm it is this building.

name: Karachi Metropolitan Corporation Building
features: Anglo-Mughal civic building in Jodhpur and Gizri sandstone with a Moorish-domed clock tower added in 1935.

photos.file: File:Karachi Municipal Corporation (KMC) Head Office at M.A Jinnah Road - Photo By Aliraza Khatri.jpg

name: Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry Building
features: Anglo-Mughal revival in sandstone with domes, faux minarets and a large arch at the front.

name: Mohatta Palace
features: Indo-Saracenic palace in pink Jodhpur and yellow Gizri stone, with nine domes and carved peacock and floral motifs.

photos.file: File:Mohatta Palace as viewed from the front.jpg

name: Frere Hall
features: Venetian-Gothic hall in yellow limestone with pointed arches, ribbed vaults, quatrefoils and flying buttresses.

name: Empress Market
features: Indo-Gothic market with vaulted roofs, multifoil arches and a 140 ft clock tower decorated with leopard heads.
note: Photo carries a caption strip and some processing.

name: Wazir Khan Mosque
by: Wazir Khan (patron), with artisans from Chiniot
features: Mughal mosque covered in kashi-kari tilework and frescoes, with four 107 ft minarets.
note: Architect unnamed in source; patron credited. Lead photo shows the entrance iwan detail, look for a full-facade shot.

name: Tomb of Shah Rukn-e-Alam
features: Three-tiered Tughluq mausoleum of red brick and shisham beams with octagonal tiers and blue tilework.

photos.file: File:Tomb of Shah Rukn e Alam, Multan.jpg

note: Second photo is a floodlit night view, use only as an extra. Architect unnamed; the article names the builder.

name: Lahore Museum
by: Bhai Ram Singh and John Lockwood Kipling
features: Indo-Saracenic red-brick museum housing Gandharan and Indus Valley collections, plus Sadequain's ceiling mural.
note: Lead photo is a side view in overcast light.

name: Karachi Port Trust Building
features: Curved yellow Jaipur-stone facade under a large central dome, mixing British, Hindu and Gothic styles.

photos.file: File:Karachi Port Trust (KPT) Head Office Building.jpg

note: Hazy light and wires in the photos; second has a black border.

name: Grand Jamia Mosque, Bahria Town
features: Four 165 ft minarets and a central dome among about 20 smaller domes; exterior clad in Multani tiles.

name: WAPDA House
features: Nine-storey block with a full-height 20 m rotunda under a plexiglas dome, three wings, and a sunken garden.
note: Office type, but a key Stone work. Gives street view across traffic.

name: Sindh Assembly Building
features: Two-floor Art Deco building that first housed the Sind Legislative Assembly.
note: no free photo (only an interior and a low-res image found)
